title: THE LAST JOURNEY
synopsis: Day 26 of the outbreak. A radio message promises one last convoy, 280 kilometres north. How much of your humanity are you willing to spend to get there?
disclaimer: Fictional scenario. Consequences are simulated for philosophical discussion.

wren.name: Wren
wren.role: A stranger with a bandaged hand

lines.text: Day 26. The highway has been quiet for three hours. Quiet is not the same as safe.
The gas station sits at the bottom of a hill, its canopy sagging, its windows long gone.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: Ten minutes. In and out. Nobody wanders off.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: We have food for four days. I would like it to be five.

lines.speaker: reed
lines.text: Then we are quick, and we are quiet.
In the van, the radio hisses. You turn it down. Then up again. The message has been on a loop since Day 22, thin as paper.

lines.speaker: broadcast
lines.text: North Haven Evacuation Center. We are accepting survivors. The final organized evacuation convoy will depart in nine days. Follow the northern route. If you can hear this message, there is still hope.
Nine days. Two hundred and eighty kilometres. You have done the sums so often that the numbers have worn smooth.

scene.caption: [Wind through the broken canopy. A distant crow.]

card.title: EMPTY SHELVES
card.text: Fictional scenario. Consequences are simulated for philosophical discussion.

lines.text: The shelves are bare, but a gas station keeps its secrets in odd places.
Look around before you decide anything. The broadcast notes are the essential reading.

items.label: The broadcast
items.title: North Haven broadcast · your notes
body: Heard on the van radio every morning since Day 22.
"The final organized convoy departs in nine days."
You wrote the count on the dashboard: nine, nine, nine, nine.
items.finding: The wording never changes. Not even the number of days.

items.label: Station ledger
items.title: Ledger behind the counter
body: Day 3: two buses at the pumps. "Going to Halden depot, then north."
Day 4: army trucks, no stop.
Day 6: nobody.
items.finding: An organized evacuation did happen, and it passed through here almost three weeks ago.

items.label: Fuel tank hatch
items.title: Underground tank hatch
body: Hatch pried open. The dipstick shows a little under a quarter.
A hand pump is chained to the pillar. The chain is rusted through.
items.finding: There is a little fuel left, if someone is willing to spend twenty minutes at a half-open hatch.

items.label: Note on the storage door
items.title: A note taped inside the storage room door
body: "Tobi — stay hidden. Don't open for anyone but me. Back before dark. Mom."
The tape is new. The handwriting is steady.
items.finding: Someone left a child here on purpose, and meant to come back.

lines.speaker: emily
lines.text: Daniel. Daniel, come here. Quietly.
She is kneeling at the storage room door. Behind a stack of flattened boxes, two eyes catch the light of her torch.

lines.speaker: tobias
lines.text: Are you the ones looking for me? Mom said someone might come.

lines.speaker: tobias
lines.text: She went to find water. She said ten minutes. That was when it was still light.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: No. We don't do this. A kid alone in a dark building, a mother who never comes back? That is bait.

lines.speaker: emily
lines.text: He is seven.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: He is dehydrated. He is not bait, Noah. He is a seven-year-old.

lines.speaker: reed
lines.text: The note on the door says she meant to come back.
They are all looking at you. They always do, now.

c1_d1.title: THE CHILD IN THE STORAGE ROOM
c1_d1.situation: A boy says his mother is nearby. Noah says it is a trap. Emily has not let go of the boy's hand. The light is going.
info: The group has food for four days.
The lot behind the station has not been checked.
Noah has the only rifle that is not jammed.

choices.label: Help the boy and look for his mother.
choices.description: Take him in, search the lot and the road, and accept the cost in time and supplies.

lines.text: You search the lot in pairs, torches low. It takes forty minutes.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: Forty minutes I will remember when we are hungry.
Because of the note, you know where to look: the cab of a truck by the fence. Sarah steers Tobias away before he can turn his head.
You find her behind the truck by the fence. Tobias sees before anyone can stop him.

lines.speaker: emily
lines.text: He has nobody now. Daniel, he has nobody.

choices.result: Tobias comes with you. The group is a little hungrier, and Emily no longer looks at you like a stranger.

choices.label: Leave immediately.
choices.description: Protect the group. Do not gamble on a stranger's story.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: Good call. Move.
Emily walks to the van without a word. The boy's eyes follow her through the gap in the boxes.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: I will remember that. Not because you were wrong. Because it was easy.

choices.result: You leave the boy behind. Noah relaxes, and Emily stops speaking to you.

choices.label: Send Leo to check the lot while the group waits.
choices.description: Someone quick checks the area. The boy stays with Sarah.

lines.speaker: leo
lines.text: I am the guy you send? Great. I have always wanted to be the guy you send.
Leo is gone twenty minutes. He comes back with a child's backpack, half a packet of crackers, and no mother.

lines.speaker: leo
lines.text: Car by the fence, empty. Whoever she was, she is long gone.
His jacket pocket is a little too full.

choices.result: Tobias stays with the group. Leo's report is too tidy, and his pockets are a little too full.

choices.label: Split the group.
choices.description: You and Emily take the boy to search. Noah, Sarah, James and Leo stay and secure the van.

lines.text: You and Emily take Tobias down the road. Behind you, the others stay with the van.
When you return, the van door is open and Noah and Sarah are not speaking. Sarah's jaw is tight; Noah's knuckles are bruised from the steering wheel.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: They were both right. That was the problem.

choices.result: Tobias comes with you. Noah and Sarah argued the whole time you were gone, and neither has forgiven the other.

lines.text: You camp in the garage, three walls and a roof. Noah takes the first watch, and does not hand it over.

lines.speaker: tobias
lines.text: Is it okay if I sleep near Emily?

lines.speaker: emily
lines.text: Yeah. Yeah, it is okay.
Emily lies awake with her face to the wall. Nobody speaks of the boy.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: Next time you split us, ask me first.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Sleep, Daniel. Tomorrow decides itself.
At dawn Sarah counts the cans twice. Then a third time.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: Four cans and half a bag of rice are gone.
The padlock on the supply crate has not been forced. It has been opened.
Four cans and half a bag of rice do not vanish. Somebody carried them. Look for the trail.

items.label: Boot prints
items.title: Prints in the dust by the crate
body: Large boot prints, size ten or eleven, from the crate to the back of the garage.
The heel of the left boot is worn on the outside edge.
items.finding: The prints match Leo's boots. The worn heel is unmistakable.

items.label: Small footprints
items.title: Footprints and a wrapper
body: Small sneaker prints, a short stride, from the crate to the storage room.
A torn corner of a ration wrapper, sticky with something sweet.
items.finding: The prints lead to where the boy sleeps. Someone has been feeding him extra.

items.label: Noah's watch log
items.title: Notes on the back of a map
body: "03:40 — noise from the garage. Checked. Nothing. Rear door ajar."
"04:10 — James asleep on his shift."
items.finding: Between 03:40 and 04:10 nobody was watching the crate. James fell asleep on his shift.

items.label: Ration count
items.title: Sarah's tally
body: Cans: eleven yesterday, seven now.
Rice: a bag and a half, now one.
items.finding: Exactly one person's share for two days. Whoever took it planned small.

c1_d2.title: WHO TOOK THE FOOD?
c1_d2.situation: The group is gathered around the empty crate. Everyone is looking at someone else.
info: Food for three days remains.
Noah wants answers before the van moves.
Every accusation will be remembered.
pressures: Fear of a thief among friends
The need to look in control

choices.label: Confront Leo in front of everyone.
choices.description: Say what you think the evidence points to, openly.

lines.speaker: leo
lines.text: Me? It is always the guy who jokes, isn't it?
Emily stares at the ground. She does not say a word.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Daniel. Are you sure?

lines.speaker: leo
lines.text: I was starving. You all had a plan for the day I fell behind, and you know it.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: He admits it. Good.

choices.result: Everyone watches you point at Leo. Whether you were right will take days to show.

choices.label: Talk quietly to Emily.
choices.description: Ask her, alone, away from the others.

lines.speaker: emily
lines.text: I gave him some of mine. And some of everyone's. I am sorry. He is so small, Daniel.

lines.speaker: emily
lines.text: You think I took it? Wow. Okay.
Behind you, across the lot, Leo is whistling. Badly.

choices.result: You and Emily talk until the light changes. What she tells you stays between you.

choices.label: Say nothing and have Noah guard the crate.
choices.description: Do not accuse anyone. Make it harder next time.

lines.text: Noah takes the crate and sits on it. Leo exhales, very slowly.
Emily's shoulders drop. She looks up at you once, and looks away.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: Your call. It is your crate, too.

choices.result: Nobody is accused. Everybody knows that you chose not to know.

choices.label: Redistribute the rations equally and move on.
choices.description: No accusation. Everyone gets less, evenly.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Fair. Hungry, but fair.

lines.speaker: leo
lines.text: Thanks, Daniel.

lines.speaker: emily
lines.text: Thank you.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: Fair does not feed anyone.

choices.result: Everyone eats a little less. Nobody is named, and the thief knows exactly how much that cost.

lines.text: You leave the station by midday. Three days of food, and a map that shrinks more slowly than you would like.
In the back seat, Tobias counts trucks that are not there. Emily counts with him.
The empty seat behind you holds the boy's shape, whether you look or not.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: Whatever we decided back there, we are going to live with it for a long time.
The radio hisses. Nine days. Nine days. Nine days.

scene.caption: [Engine hum. Tyres on cracked asphalt.]

lines.text: Day 28. The town is called Brook Hollow, according to a sign with three bullet holes in it.
Smoke rises from the old grain mill. Someone has been burning wood, which means someone has been alive.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: Hands where I can see them.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Easy. We are the same as you, only with more soup.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: A hot meal, a roof, a few things to trade. We ask nothing. Well. Almost nothing.

lines.speaker: tobias
lines.text: Is that real soup?
Eleven survivors, a fortified mill, a rule about knives at the door. They are kind the way people are kind when they have something to protect.

scene.caption: [A distant generator. Voices behind a wall.]

card.title: STRANGERS
card.text: Kindness has a price. The question is who pays it.

lines.text: Marcus gives you the run of the camp. Look before you thank anyone.

items.label: Marcus's offer
items.title: Terms, as Marcus states them
body: He says the last line quickly.
items.finding: A fair trade on paper. Ammunition is the one thing you cannot easily replace.

items.label: Supply shed
items.title: Depot stamps in the supply shed
body: Stacked cans stamped HALDEN REGIONAL DEPOT, hundreds of them.
Marcus told you they were scraping by.
items.finding: They have far more than they admit. They are not desperate. They are careful.

items.label: North gate
items.title: Rusted wire at the north gate
body: Fresh blood on a rusted barbed-wire fence.
Beside it, a ripped glove, a woman's size.
items.finding: Wren's hand may have been cut here on old wire. Not a bite. But nobody saw it happen.

items.label: Marcus's logbook
items.title: Logbook of the mill
body: Arrivals and departures, in a neat hand.
"Day 22: Wren, arrived alone." "Day 25: Mira, left in the night." "Day 27: Cal, left."
items.finding: People leave this place in the night. Marcus writes it down as if it were normal.

lines.text: At the long table, Wren passes the bread with her left hand. The right is wrapped to the wrist in grey cloth.
Sarah has seen it too. She leans toward you and is silent for a moment.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: That cloth is clean at the edge and dark in the middle. I have seen that pattern before. In the first week.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.text: It is nothing. Caught it on a gate.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: Say it out loud or I will.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: If it is a bite, we leave before dark.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Be careful what you accuse a person of at a stranger's table.

c2_d3.title: THE BANDAGED HAND
c2_d3.situation: Sarah thinks the injury might be a bite. Wren says she caught it on a gate. Eleven strangers are listening.
info: A bite takes one to two days to show.
Marcus's people are armed.
You have not seen the wound.
pressures: Hospitality you do not want to lose

choices.label: Tell everyone about the suspicious injury.
choices.description: Say it openly, in the hall.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: You walk into my house and call my guest a corpse?

lines.speaker: wren
lines.text: Show them. Go on.
She does not unwrap it. Nobody eats. The soup goes cold.

choices.result: The mill falls silent. You have said the word nobody wanted to hear.

choices.label: Ask Sarah to examine Wren privately.
choices.description: Midnight, one quiet look. No audience.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: It is a cut. Deep, dirty, rusted. But a cut. Not a bite.
Neither of you notices that Wren is awake.

choices.result: Sarah examines the wound in secret: a cut, not a bite. But Wren knows she was examined.

choices.label: Trust Wren and accept Marcus's help.
choices.description: Eat, rest, trade. Do not ask.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: There. That is how neighbours do it.

lines.speaker: leo
lines.text: Soup, Daniel. Soup!

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: I hope you are right.

choices.result: The trade is made. Everyone eats well, and Sarah does not.

choices.label: Hide your suspicion to avoid a panic.
choices.description: Accept the help. Keep an eye on the hand yourself.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: You looked straight at me and decided I was imagining it.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: If she turns tonight, that is on you.

choices.result: The hospitality stays warm. Sarah and Noah go cold.

lines.text: Night in the mill. Walls, a fire, the sound of other people breathing. For the first time in weeks you sleep with your boots off.
Marcus's people watch the door, not the road.
You wake before dawn. There is a gap in the line of sleeping bags.

scene.caption: [A fire settling. A door on its hinge.]

lines.text: Wren's bedroll is empty and neatly folded. Her boots are gone. The north gate is unbarred.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: She left. I would think about why.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: She heard something last night. Two of you whispering by her bed.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: If she is out there with that hand, alone...
Leo's bedroll is empty. His boots are gone. So is a box of your ammunition.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: I told you. Did I not tell you?

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Let us decide nothing before we know.
Tobias's blanket is thrown back. His shoes are by the wall.

lines.speaker: emily
lines.text: He would not go anywhere without his shoes. Daniel, please.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: Cold floor. He cannot have gone far.

c2_d4.title: SOMEONE IS MISSING
c2_d4.situation: Someone is gone. Whatever happened, it happened quietly, and the mill is awake and watching you.
info: Dawn is an hour away.
The north gate is unbarred.
Marcus's people are armed and watching.

choices.label: Search immediately.
choices.description: Go out in the dark. It costs ammunition and nerves.

lines.text: You find Wren at the roadside, shaking, her wrapped hand held to her chest. She lets Sarah look.
You find Leo at the gate, bargaining with two of Marcus's men. He is trading your ammunition for food. He looks ashamed. And fed.
You find Tobias in the cellar, curled up beside the water barrels. He followed the sound of a dripping tap.

lines.speaker: emily
lines.text: Thank you. Thank you. Thank you.

choices.result: You find them. It costs you sleep and ammunition, but nobody is left out in the dark.

choices.label: Wait for daylight.
choices.description: Do not risk anyone else in the dark.

lines.text: At first light a scavenger brings Wren's glove to the gate. Nothing else.
Leo walks back in at dawn, whistling, carrying two sacks. "I got us a deal." The sacks are heavy. So is the silence.
Tobias is found at dawn in the cellar, pale and silent. He will not say what he saw.

lines.speaker: emily
lines.text: You waited. He was down there for hours.

choices.result: Daylight comes, and so does what the night left behind.

choices.label: Confront Marcus.
choices.description: Ask him directly what happened under his roof.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: You think I take people? I count people. That is different.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Take the antibiotics and go. Consider the debt paid.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: He is lying about something.

choices.result: Marcus gives you medicine to leave quickly. Nobody believes his answers.

choices.label: Move on without them.
choices.description: The road does not wait. Nine days is not a lot.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: Good. We lose a day, we lose everyone.
Emily does not look at you. Sarah does not look at anything.

choices.result: You leave without looking back. Behind you the mill closes its gate.

lines.text: You leave Brook Hollow with the sun low and the radio quiet. Behind you, a thin line of smoke.
Wren walks a little behind the van, carrying a pack she has no right to carry, and nobody tells her to stop.
Marcus's men shadow you to the edge of the town, rifles lowered but ready.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Kindness and caution are not opposites. People forget that.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: Something is wrong with this road. I cannot say what.
Day 30. The van coughs twice, shudders, and dies on a forest road a kilometre from anywhere.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: Cracked coolant hose. We are not driving on this.

lines.speaker: reed
lines.text: Give me an hour.
The fuel needle has been lying on empty since yesterday. You tell nobody.
Nobody mentions the food. Everybody counts it.
The trees close over the road like a held breath.

scene.caption: [A cooling engine ticking. Wind in tall pines.]

card.title: NO WAY BACK
card.text: When the road stops, the group has to decide what it is made of.

lines.text: You need a part, a plan and a place to sleep. Start with what is in front of you.

items.label: Engine bay
items.title: Under the bonnet
body: Coolant hose split along the seam.
A part from a similar model might fit: the wrecked van two hundred metres up the road.
items.finding: A replacement hose from the wreck would fix it. That means going into the trees.

items.label: Road map
items.title: A hunting map in the glovebox
body: A lodge marked two kilometres east.
Red pen: "safe room — see sign."
items.finding: A lodge two kilometres east: shelter, if you can reach it before dark.

items.label: Tracks
items.title: Marks in the mud
body: Drag marks. Many feet. Heading toward the wreck.
items.finding: The infected move in numbers here. The wreck is not empty.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: Two go, quiet. Two cover. The rest hold the van. Nobody improvises.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: And if there is a bite? We have no way to know in the dark.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Then we will look at each other and decide. Together.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: Fine. Then do it yourself.

lines.speaker: emily
lines.text: I can go. I am small. I am fast.
Every plan has a cost, and the cost has a face.

c3_d5.title: WHO GOES INTO THE TREES?
c3_d5.situation: You need a hose from the wreck. Something moves in the trees beyond it, and whoever goes cannot be protected by the others.
info: Ammunition is scarce, and your choices made it so.
Nightfall is in three hours.
The lodge is two kilometres east.

choices.label: Go yourself, with Noah.
choices.description: You and Noah take the rifle. The others hold the van.

lines.text: The wreck is a tomb of broken glass. The hose comes free in four minutes. The fifth minute is the problem.
Three of them come out of the ferns at once. Noah drops two. The third goes down on top of you both, and when you shove it off there is blood on the ground and you are not sure whose it is.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: I am fine. Go. Go.

choices.result: You return with the hose. Noah is quiet. There is blood on somebody's sleeve.

choices.label: Send Leo and Emily.
choices.description: Fast and quiet. They are light and quick.

lines.text: You wait at the van and count shots. Three. A pause. Then one more.
Emily comes back first, white-faced, with the hose. Leo limps behind her, laughing a little too loudly, his trouser leg torn "by a branch".
Leo is not with her. Emily keeps her sleeve pulled down to the knuckles and will not say where he went. He turns up an hour later, out of breath, saying he ran for help.

choices.result: You have the hose. You also have the sense that one of them is not telling you something.

choices.label: Send Noah and Leo.
choices.description: A soldier and a runner. You stay with the others.

lines.text: Noah comes back alone, carrying the hose, his left forearm wrapped in his shirt.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: Scratched on a branch. Leo ran. He ran, Daniel. I told you.

choices.result: Noah brings the hose and a story about a branch. Leo is somewhere in the trees.

choices.label: Nobody goes. Push the van to the lodge.
choices.description: No splitting up. Everybody pushes, for two kilometres.

lines.text: You push for two hours. The infected find you on the last hill.
James, at the back of the van, slows. A hand closes on his arm. By the time the shots stop, he is pale and silent and holding his ribs.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Just winded. I am an old man, Daniel.

choices.result: The van reaches the lodge. Everyone is alive, and James is breathing very carefully.

lines.text: The lodge is cold, dark, and has a door that locks. Tonight you barricade it. Tomorrow you fix the van.
Noah sits apart, cleaning his rifle with his left hand only.
Leo laughs a little too loudly and keeps his leg out of the firelight.
Emily keeps her sleeve pulled down to the knuckles and eats nothing.
James takes the last seat, breathing hard, one hand pressed to his ribs.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: Somebody is hiding something. I know that look. I wore it.

scene.caption: [A fire crackling. Something moving outside, far off.]

c3_d6.title: STILL OUT THERE
c3_d6.situation: One of your own is not back. The trees are dark, and there is no telling what is out there with them.
info: Noah has the only working rifle.
The lodge door is already barricaded.
Ammunition is thin.

choices.label: Go back for them now.
choices.description: Torches low, three of you into the dark.

lines.text: You find Emily sitting on the fallen trunk, shaking, the hose still in her fist. She lets you take her hand.
You find Leo behind a boulder with his knees drawn up. He does not look at you. "I froze," he says. "I just froze."

choices.result: You walk back into the dark and bring them out. It costs ammunition. It buys something harder to count.

choices.label: Wait until dawn.
choices.description: Nobody else goes out in the dark.

lines.text: At first light there is a knock, quiet, three times. Emily stands there, pale as paper, and walks past you without a word.
At first light Leo is on the step, grey with cold, refusing to meet anyone's eyes.

choices.result: They come back by themselves. It is not the same as being brought back.

choices.label: Send Noah alone.
choices.description: He is the best of you at this.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: Twenty minutes. If I am not back, do not come looking.
He is back in nineteen, carrying one of them over his shoulder.

choices.result: Noah brings them back. He says it was nothing. His hands say otherwise.

choices.label: Close the door and keep going at first light.
choices.description: You cannot risk everyone for one.

lines.text: Nobody sleeps. At dawn you open the door. There is no one on the step.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: You made the choice a captain makes. I hope you can keep making it.

choices.result: The door stays closed. In the morning, the step is empty.

lines.text: The lodge has a washroom, a medicine cabinet, a guest book and a sink with pink water in it.

items.label: Torn sleeve
items.title: A sleeve washed in the sink
body: A torn sleeve, wrung out and hung over the tap. The water in the basin is still pink.
items.finding: Someone washed a wound here tonight. Whose arm was it?

items.label: ID badge
items.title: A badge by the sink
body: Riverside General Hospital · S. MILLER, RN · Pediatric ICU.
Sarah told you she worked at a rural clinic.
items.finding: This badge says she worked somewhere else, and with children.

items.label: Guest book
items.title: Entries in the guest book
body: "We heard the broadcast too. Heading to North Haven. If you read this, do not take the main road. — the Alvarez family, Day 24."
items.finding: Another group went north ten days ago and wrote: not the main road.

items.label: Medicine cabinet
items.title: The cabinet by the door
body: Bandages, antiseptic, a blister of old antibiotics.
items.finding: Not much, but it is more than you had.

c3_d7.title: THE ONE WHO IS HIDING
c3_d7.situation: Somebody in this lodge has been bitten and is hiding it. Sarah says the first hours matter. Everyone else is already looking at everyone else.
info: A bite shows in one to two days.
The lodge has a cellar with a lock.
Whatever you decide, everyone will see it.

choices.label: Isolate the person you suspect.
choices.description: Lock them in the cellar until Sarah can examine them.

lines.text: You ask quietly. They go down the cellar steps without arguing. Their back is very straight.

lines.speaker: leo
lines.text: Me? Because I joke? Because I ran? Okay. Okay, Daniel.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: If you are wrong, you have just locked up an innocent man.

choices.result: The door closes. The lodge is quieter, and not at all calmer.

choices.label: Examine everyone together, in the open.
choices.description: Sarah checks every arm and every leg. No exceptions, including you.

lines.text: Sleeves up, trouser legs up, one by one, under the lamp. Nobody speaks.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: Here. It is not a scratch.
The room moves a half-step away from them.

choices.result: Everyone sees. Nobody can pretend afterwards that they did not.

choices.label: Examine them privately with Sarah.
choices.description: A quiet word, and a quiet look. Nobody else needs to know yet.

lines.text: You and Sarah take the bitten one to the washroom. The tap runs a long time.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: Thirty-six hours. Maybe forty-eight. I am sorry.
They thank you. Nobody should have to thank you for that.

choices.result: Only you, Sarah and the bitten one know. It is a secret three people have to carry.

choices.label: Trust them. Do not ask.
choices.description: Give everyone the dignity of silence, and hope the silence holds.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: There is a kind of trust that is just fear wearing a nicer coat.
Nobody sleeps well. Everybody keeps one eye on the same corner of the room.

choices.result: Nothing is said. Everyone knows that something is.

lines.text: Before dawn, Noah takes Sarah's jacket from the hook to cover a window. The badge slides out of the pocket and rings on the floor.
You have already seen the badge. The hook, the jacket and her silence all make sense now.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: Riverside General. Pediatric ICU. That is not a clinic in the country, Sarah.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: No. It is not.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: Day eleven. A ward of children and one fire door. I had a choice about who went through it. I took the ones I could carry.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: I told you I never left a patient. It was easier than telling you which one I left.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: You lied to us.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: She told us the truth now. That is not nothing.
Nobody sleeps again. By morning the van is fixed, and the group is not.

scene.caption: [A hinge. A held breath. Rain starting on the roof.]

lines.text: Noah asks to be left at the next crossroads. He says it like an order.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: I will hold the road behind you. That is the one thing I am good for. Let me be good for it.
Leo tells the group himself, in the end, with a joke that falls flat. Then he stops making jokes.

lines.speaker: leo
lines.text: Tell Emily I was brave, okay? Tell her I was funny and brave.
Emily rolls her sleeve up before anyone asks. Her voice does not shake. Her hands do.

lines.speaker: emily
lines.text: I wanted to be useful. That is all I wanted. Can I be useful now?
James says it plainly: he is not going to make the next hill. He asks for the teacher's privilege, a last lesson.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Do not mistake survival for living. They are cousins. They are not twins.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: You and I decided this alone, Daniel. The others will ask why.
In the night the sleeping bag beside Noah goes very still, and then it does not. It takes four shots and one long second.
Leo goes first. He was laughing three minutes ago. There is no time to be gentle, and nobody is.
Emily wakes screaming, and it is not a dream. Sarah is closest. Sarah does not look away.
James is found at dawn in his chair, cold and still, one hand pressed to his ribs, and for a moment you hope. Then you see the chair is soaked.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: If you had let me look, it would not have happened like this.
Nobody says the name for a while. Then everybody does.

scene.caption: [A single shot. Then wind.]

lines.text: Day 32. Riverside General Hospital rises out of the fog with its windows black and its car park full of abandoned ambulances.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: I know this door. I know which stair is loose. I know exactly where I stood.

lines.speaker: reed
lines.text: We need medicine, a quiet room, and information. We are not here for the past.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: Then you do not know what this building is.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: Eyes up. Hospitals are never empty.
The doors open on a dark atrium. At the bottom of the stairs, someone has painted a single word: STAY.

scene.caption: [A drip. A ceiling tile shifting. Distant static.]

card.title: THE HOSPITAL
card.text: Some places keep the truth. Others keep the people who would tell it.

lines.text: Offices, wards, a radio room, a pharmacy cage. Evacuations leave paper behind.

items.label: Evacuation board
items.title: Convoy manifests on a corkboard
body: HALDEN → NORTH HAVEN. Manifests pinned in rows.
Last loading: Day 21, 06:00.
items.finding: The organized evacuation left on Day 21. Today is Day 32.

items.label: Dictaphone
items.title: A tape in the radio room
body: Recorded loop: the North Haven message, then static, then the same message again.
A label in marker: "LOOPED DAY 9 — M."
items.finding: The message you have been following is a recording, looped since Day 9. The nine days never counted down.

items.label: Infection memo
items.title: Infection protocol memo
body: Onset 36–48 hours. No known treatment.
North Haven protocol: 72-hour quarantine for all arrivals. A bite means no entry.
items.finding: North Haven screens and quarantines. Anyone bitten will be refused.

items.label: Security office
items.title: A locker in the security office
body: A guard's locker, forced open long ago. Under a coat: a box of rifle rounds, almost full.
items.finding: Somebody died here with their ammunition unspent. It is yours now.

items.label: Pharmacy cage
items.title: Behind the register
body: The cage is open and most shelves are bare. Behind the register: two sealed boxes.
items.finding: Two boxes of antibiotics and one of dressings. Enough to matter.

items.label: Pediatric ward chart
items.title: Chart on the ward wall
body: Bed 4: Lily H., eight. Status: evacuated Day 3 — North Haven (Halden bus).
Pinned beside it: a child's drawing of a woman in blue.
items.finding: Lily was not left to die. She was put on an early bus. If North Haven still stands, she may be alive there.

lines.text: A door opens on the third floor. A woman in a stained coat steps into the torchlight, thin as a coat hanger.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: Anna? Anna Cole? They said you did not leave the ICU.

lines.speaker: anna
lines.text: I did not leave. Then I did. Hello, Sarah. You look like you slept.

lines.speaker: anna
lines.text: I went north. Day twenty-eight. The gate was shut. They turned us away, a whole bus of us, no more beds. I came back here to die, I suppose.

lines.speaker: anna
lines.text: North Haven is not taking anyone, Daniel. Whatever the radio says.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: She is lying, or she is mistaken. The message says there is still hope.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: The message says what it said on Day nine. Have we asked ourselves why it has not changed?

c4_d8.title: THE WOMAN FROM THE ICU
c4_d8.situation: Anna says North Haven is closed. The radio says it is open. You have two stories and nine days that may already be fewer.
info: Anna has no reason to lie, and no reason to be believed.
The hospital radio still has power.
You have found documents that complicate both stories.

choices.label: Believe Anna and rethink the journey.
choices.description: If the gate is shut, you need another plan before you walk into a rifle.

lines.speaker: anna
lines.text: Thank you. I was beginning to think nobody believed anything any more.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: You are throwing away our only plan on the word of a stranger.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: It is the first sensible thing we have done in days.

choices.result: You decide to treat the gate as closed until it proves otherwise.

choices.label: Ignore her and follow the original coordinates.
choices.description: The broadcast is all you have. Do not let one story undo it.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: Good. We have been given a destination. A man needs a destination.

lines.speaker: anna
lines.text: Then I hope you are right. I really do.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: You did not even ask her what she saw.

choices.result: The plan stays the same. The doubt does not.

choices.label: Search for more evidence before deciding.
choices.description: Go through the radio room properly. It costs time and risk, and you may find what you hoped not to.

lines.text: You spend an hour in the radio room with a torch and a stubborn hope. The tape is where Anna said it would be, and so is the label in marker.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: The message is a recording. Someone wanted it kept playing.

lines.speaker: anna
lines.text: Now you see why I did not argue.

choices.result: You find out what the message really is, and you cannot un-know it.

choices.label: Use the hospital radio to call North Haven.
choices.description: Ask them yourselves. If anyone answers, you will know.

lines.text: The set wakes with a groan. You find the frequency from the loop and press the key.

lines.speaker: reed
lines.text: North Haven, this is Daniel Reed. Six survivors, approaching from the south. Do you copy?
Static. Then a long, listening silence.

choices.result: You send the call into the dark. Somewhere, the dark is listening.

c4_d9.title: TEN MINUTES ON THE THIRD FLOOR
c4_d9.situation: Sarah asks for ten minutes in the pediatric ward. She does not say why. Everybody knows.
info: The third floor has not been checked.
Ten minutes is a long time in a building like this.
Sarah will go with or without permission.
pressures: Guilt that is not yours to settle

choices.label: Go with her.
choices.description: You stand beside her at the door. It costs ammunition and a bit of your own nerve.

lines.text: The ward is clean, and horribly quiet. Sarah goes to bed four and stands there a long time.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: She was not here. She was not here, Daniel. They took her.
Sarah laughs once, and then she cries, and then you hold the door.

choices.result: Sarah finds what she came for. She stops carrying it alone.

choices.label: Let her go alone, and hold the stairs.
choices.description: Give her the privacy, and guard the way back.

lines.text: You hold the stairs for eleven minutes. Something bangs, far off, and stops.
Sarah comes down holding her left arm. She says nothing. She nods once.
Sarah comes down with her face washed and her hands steady. She nods once.

choices.result: You give her the ward and keep the stairs. It is the right size of trust.

choices.label: Refuse. Not here.
choices.description: The building is dangerous and the group comes first.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: Ten minutes. I carried this for twenty-one days. You could have given me ten minutes.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: The leader is right. Nobody gets lost in here.

choices.result: You keep the group together. Sarah does not forgive the price.

lines.text: You are loading the van when the radio room speaker coughs and wakes.

lines.speaker: elise
lines.text: North Haven Control to unknown party. Identify yourselves. Identify yourselves, or cut the channel.

lines.speaker: elise
lines.text: North Haven Control. We received your call. Who is speaking?

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: No. That is...

lines.speaker: elise
lines.text: Noah? Noah Carter? Is that you? You are supposed to be dead.
Noah does not move. He is looking at the speaker as if it were a person.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: I know that voice. Elise Carter. Noah's sister. He told us once, years ago, before everything.

lines.speaker: elise
lines.text: Listen carefully. The gate is open to screened groups only. The convoy left on the twenty-first. Do not bring anyone who is bitten.

lines.speaker: reed
lines.text: Your broadcast is a recording. It has not changed since Day nine.

lines.speaker: elise
lines.text: I know. I could not stop it. The transmitter is in the tower, and the tower is not mine.
The channel goes dead. In the quiet, nobody looks at anybody.

scene.caption: [Radio static. A distant speaker.]

lines.text: Day 34. A concrete barricade, two burned-out buses, a handwritten sign: TOLL. Rifles on the roofs say what the sign does not.

lines.speaker: voss
lines.text: Three pass. Healthy, armed, or useful. The rest wait, or leave. I do not make the rules. I just carry them out.

lines.speaker: reed
lines.text: North Haven expects us. We spoke to them.

lines.speaker: voss
lines.text: Everyone says North Haven expects them.
A familiar voice from the barricade: "That one is all right. I would stake my hand on it." Wren, thinner, with a rifle slung over her good shoulder.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: The sick are not allowed through. We all heard her say it.

scene.caption: [Wind on corrugated iron. A bolt sliding home.]

card.title: THE CHECKPOINT
card.text: The last wall before the last wall.

lines.text: While Voss confers with his lieutenants, you have a few minutes among the barricades and your own people's bags.

items.label: Pass list
items.title: The posted toll rules
body: Pinned to the barricade, in marker.
items.finding: The pass favours skills: a nurse and a mechanic would qualify. A teacher would not.

items.label: James's notebook
items.title: A radio notebook from James's pack
body: "Day 27: North Haven closed to new arrivals by order of the council. Convoy left Day 24. I could not tell them."
"The gate takes screened people only. It is a lottery. If I say it, it breaks the group."
items.finding: James has known for days. He has been walking you toward a gate he knew might be closed.

items.label: Barricade graffiti
items.title: Marker on the concrete
body: "Gate open 6–8 am only." "Leave the sick. They will know."
items.finding: The gate has hours. The screening finds what people hide.

items.label: Culvert map
items.title: A hand-drawn map from the guest book's page
body: A maintenance tunnel under the checkpoint, marked "Alvarez — safe."
items.finding: There is a way under the barricade, if you know it exists.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: I should have told you. I have been trying to say it for four days.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: You found the notebook. Then you know. I was afraid it would break us.
James says nothing. He has not looked at you since the hospital.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: And I knew about the screening. Elise told me in the spring: whoever is sick does not get in. I did not say so either.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: So we have all been carrying something. Fine. We can put it down here, or we can walk under it.
There is no time left for more truth than this.

c5_d10.title: THE TOLL
c5_d10.situation: Voss will let three of you through. You are six, counting the ones who have not said what they know. The road behind you is not safe either.
info: The gate hours are short.
Your ammunition and food are your only currency.
Someone on the roof has you in their sights.
pressures: The shadow of those left behind

choices.label: Negotiate with Voss.
choices.description: Pay what you can and ask for everyone. It depends on what you still have.

lines.speaker: voss
lines.text: Three magazines and a day of food, and the lot of you go through. That is my last number.

lines.speaker: voss
lines.text: That is not enough. I can take three of you. Not six.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.text: Voss. Let them through. I owe them my hand.

choices.result: A price is named. Whether you can pay it depends on every choice that brought you here.

choices.label: Split the group.
choices.description: Let three pass and hope the rest can follow another way.

lines.text: You choose three. Emily asks who the other three are. Nobody answers.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Choosing is the cruelty. Not the choice itself. The choosing.

choices.result: Three go forward, three wait. The distance between them is longer than the barricade.

choices.label: Look for another way around.
choices.description: Through the woods or under the wall, if you know there is a way.

lines.text: You leave the road. Behind you the barricade becomes a grey line and then nothing.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: If this goes wrong, it goes wrong in the dark.

choices.result: You go around. It costs time, and the road is not empty.

choices.label: Break through by force.
choices.description: Use what you have. It will not be quiet, and it will not be forgotten.

lines.text: It takes ninety seconds. Afterwards the barricade is quiet, and nobody can say it is the quiet you wanted.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: They had families. Voss had a daughter. I saw her drawing taped to the booth.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: You did what had to be done.

choices.result: The barricade is yours. You do not look at what is left of it.

lines.text: The culvert is a concrete throat, knee-deep in cold water. Your torch finds a child's shoe, and then a chalk arrow, and then another.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Alvarez. The family from the guest book. They made it through here.
Above you, faintly, a muffled roar: the checkpoint, and something very large approaching it.
You skirt the checkpoint through dead pines. Twice you stop and lie flat while something dragging its feet crosses the path.
You are scratched, tired, and a bullet lighter. You come out near the checkpoint from the wrong side.
The sound arrives before the sight: a low grinding, like a river under ice. Then the road goes dark with them.

lines.speaker: voss
lines.text: Everyone inside. Everyone. Close the gate.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: Hundreds. We cannot stop that with what we have.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: Daniel. Whatever you are going to do, do it now.
Every face turns to you, the way faces always do.

scene.caption: [A low grinding roar, getting louder.]

c5_d11.title: THE SURGE
c5_d11.situation: A mass of infected is coming down the road. Everyone here will die unless someone decides now.
info: Ammunition will decide some of this.
Fuel will decide some of the rest.
Someone has to go first.

choices.label: Hold the barricade and fight.
choices.description: Stand and shoot. It depends on how much you have left.

lines.text: You hold for eleven minutes. The magazine counter on Noah's rifle is a number nobody says aloud.
The line holds. The road is carpeted. There is silence, and then there is a breath.
The ammunition runs out before the road does.
The line breaks. By the time the road clears, Leo is gone.

choices.result: The barricade holds, or it does not. What it costs depends on what you kept.

choices.label: Draw them away with the van and the horn.
choices.description: You drive, alone, past the front of the crowd. It costs fuel. It might cost more.

lines.text: You lean on the horn and drive into the grey tide, and the grey tide turns, slow as a ship, to follow.
You come back two hours later, scratched down one forearm, with the tank dry and the road clear.
You come back two hours later, shaking, with the tank dry and the road clear.
The van coughs on the last of its fuel and you finish the run on foot, with the horn still ringing behind you. You come back at dawn, scratched and alive.
The tank is dry before you reach the road. You do not come back.

reaction.caption: [A horn. An engine under strain. Fading.]

choices.result: You buy the group a road at the price of the van, and perhaps more.

choices.label: Someone has to stay at the gate. Let them volunteer.
choices.description: Do not choose. Ask. And be ready for who answers.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: I will. It is what I am for.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: No. Not him. It should be the old man. It is always better to have taught than to be taught.

lines.speaker: leo
lines.text: I... I can. I can do it. Somebody has to, right?
Nobody argues. That is the worst part.

reaction.caption: [The grinding roar. A single clear voice.]

choices.result: Somebody stays. The others walk away from the sound.

choices.label: Open the gate for everyone, including Voss's people.
choices.description: Run together. Everyone for everyone.

lines.speaker: voss
lines.text: You would open my gate for my own people?
The checkpoint dissolves into a column of strangers running the same way.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: This is what survival looks like when it learns to share.

choices.result: You run together, every shape of survivor. It costs food and bullets. It buys something else.

lines.text: Night, on a ridge. Far below, a wall of light: floodlights on concrete, a lit gate, the glitter of wire.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: North Haven. It is real.

lines.speaker: emily
lines.text: It is so bright. I forgot that light could be bright.
You pull your sleeve down over the scratch. Nobody sees. Or nobody says.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: Tomorrow, then. Whatever we are tomorrow, we will be it together.

scene.caption: [A far-off siren. Wind. A single dog barking.]

lines.text: Day 35. North Haven is not a paradise. It is a wall, a gate, a queue, and a great many people trying to look like they are not afraid.

lines.speaker: okafor
lines.text: Welcome to North Haven. Please do not touch the wire. Please keep your hands where we can see them.

lines.speaker: elise
lines.text: Noah. You came. You actually came.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: I said I would, Lise. I said I would, years ago.

lines.speaker: elise
lines.text: You are Reed. I have heard your voice. The one that said the broadcast was a recording.
The gate is open six hours a day. The queue behind you is forty people long, and none of them look at each other.

scene.caption: [A heavy gate on a rail. Quiet voices. A loudspeaker, far off.]

card.title: THE LAST JOURNEY
card.text: The road ends here. What comes after is a different kind of road.

lines.text: While the gate is still shut, you have a few minutes with what is posted on it.

items.label: Posted rules
items.title: Rules at the gate
body: Printed on a laminated sheet, with a bullet hole through the middle.
items.finding: The wall holds two thousand. Every new arrival means one fewer bed for someone already inside.

items.label: The queue
items.title: The line at the gate
body: Forty people ahead of you, thin and quiet.
Nobody talks about the ones who were not let in.
items.finding: The queue moves slowly. In practice it is a lottery, and everyone in it knows.

items.label: Names wall
items.title: Marker on the concrete
body: Hundreds of names in marker, in many hands.
Near the bottom: "Lily H. — Ward C."
items.finding: Lily's name is on the wall. She arrived on the early bus. She is alive, or was.

items.label: Gate radio channel
items.title: The tower frequency
body: The gate operator leaves the tower frequency open.
The looped message is still playing, to everyone.
items.finding: You could cut the loop and broadcast what you know. Others are still walking toward a gate that is closed to them.

lines.speaker: okafor
lines.text: Screening is simple. Arms, legs, neck. A blood test. If you are clean you are in quarantine for three days, then you are in.

lines.speaker: okafor
lines.text: If you are not clean, I cannot let you in. I do not make that rule. I enforce it. Please do not make me.
You can feel the scratch on your forearm like a second pulse.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: Daniel. Show them your arm.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: Whatever you decide, I will stand where you stand.
Everyone here has a number written on their face, and none of the numbers are good.

c6_d13.title: THE SCREENING
c6_d13.situation: The gate is open, and the screening begins in ten minutes. Everything you have learned, and everything you have hidden, comes due now.
info: The screening finds what people hide.
Elise Carter is somewhere inside.
The tower frequency is open.
pressures: What you owe the people still on the road

choices.label: Submit everyone to the screening, honestly.
choices.description: Hide nothing and trust the process.

lines.speaker: okafor
lines.text: Thank you. It is rare. Most people shake as though they had something to hide.
The scanner finds the scratch in nine seconds.

lines.speaker: okafor
lines.text: I am sorry. I am so very sorry.

choices.result: You tell the truth, all of it, and let the gate decide.

choices.label: Hide Daniel's scratch.
choices.description: Sleeves down, eyes forward, no questions.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: If they find it, they will not just refuse you. They will put the rest of us in quarantine with you.
You roll the sleeve down. Your pulse is in your ears.

choices.result: You gamble that nobody will look closely.

choices.label: Ask for Elise Carter and negotiate with what you know.
choices.description: You have a name, a story and some evidence. Use them.

lines.speaker: elise
lines.text: I cannot waive the screening. I can speak for you. I can say I know your voice.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.text: Lise. Please.

lines.speaker: elise
lines.text: All of you. If every one of you passes.

choices.result: You spend your credit with someone who owes you nothing.

choices.label: Cut the loop and broadcast the truth.
choices.description: Use the open tower channel to tell everyone on the road what you found.

lines.text: The tower operator is looking at his hands. You say his name. He nods, once.

lines.speaker: reed
lines.text: This is Daniel Reed. The message you have been following is a recording. Here is what is true.

choices.result: You put the truth on the air, and the air carries it.

choices.label: Walk away. There is nothing here worth the price.
choices.description: A wall is a wall, whichever side you are on.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: There is a kind of courage in turning around. It does not get medals.
Behind you, the gate keeps its six hours.

choices.result: You leave the queue. Somebody behind you takes your place and does not look at you.

lines.text: You see it a second too late: Leo, at the guard post, talking low to a man with a clipboard.

lines.speaker: leo
lines.text: I am clean. I am clean and I have ammunition. They are not clean. Look at his arm. Look at hers.

lines.speaker: leo
lines.text: You wronged me, Daniel. In front of everyone. I did not take that food.

lines.speaker: leo
lines.text: You named me in front of everyone. And you were right. And I never forgave you.

lines.speaker: leo
lines.text: You all looked at me like I was the one who would run. So I ran. Toward the only door.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: Leo. Please.
The gate does not open for you. It opens for him, and closes again.

scene.caption: [A heavy bolt. Boots on concrete.]

c6_d14.title: THE LAST CHOICE
c6_d14.situation: The gate is open. Whatever happens next, you chose it, and so did everyone you brought this far.
info: The wall holds two thousand people.
Whoever is not let in has nowhere to go.
Everyone is watching you.
pressures: A future that is not yours alone

choices.label: Walk in together.
choices.description: Everyone who is left, side by side.

lines.text: The gate opens in a long, quiet scrape. Nobody says anything. You go through in the order you arrived.

choices.result: You take the last steps with everyone beside you.

choices.label: Stay outside so the others can enter.
choices.description: If the gate has one condition, you can be the one it names.

lines.speaker: reed
lines.text: Go. I will be here when you come back.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: No. No. Daniel, please.

choices.result: You step back from the gate and let the others go on without you.

choices.label: Enter alone.
choices.description: One place, one name, one bed. You can take it.

lines.text: The guard checks your name against a list. It is on the list. It is the only one.

lines.speaker: okafor
lines.text: You are the only one who passes. I am sorry for the rest.

choices.result: You walk through alone, and the gate closes behind you with a sound you will hear for the rest of your life.

choices.label: Turn away and build somewhere new.
choices.description: Take the people you have and the tools you have, and find a place nobody has a wall around yet.

lines.speaker: james
lines.text: There is a hill, two valleys back. A spring. Good soil.
You turn the van around. Nobody speaks. Then someone laughs, once.

choices.result: You turn your back on the wall.

TOGETHER.title: TOGETHER
TOGETHER.subtitle: They walked in together. Not all of them walked all the way.
TOGETHER.result: The gate opens for the group, one by one, under the lights. Behind you, the road is full of names. You have reached safety together, and the journey has cost more than you can count.
TOGETHER.unresolved: Everyone who is left is inside. Who decides what the ones who are not were worth?

lines.text: The gate opens in a long, quiet scrape. You walk through it in the order you arrived.

lines.speaker: okafor

THE_SACRIFICE.title: THE SACRIFICE
THE_SACRIFICE.subtitle: One name stayed outside the wall.
THE_SACRIFICE.result: Daniel stays outside so the remaining survivors can enter North Haven. The gate closes behind them. The road ahead of you, as the light goes, is the same road you have always known.
THE_SACRIFICE.unresolved: Does a leader's death settle what he owed the people he led, or does it only excuse him from living with it?

conflicts.TOGETHER: Kant and Mill agree that the group mattered and disagree about what it permits. Kant would count the lost as persons, Mill as part of a sum. Aristotle asks whether the bond that held the group was one of use or of goodwill.
conflicts.THE_SACRIFICE: Here the theories pull in different directions. Mill can justify the sacrifice by its results, Kant questions whether a person may be spent even by their own choice, and Aristotle asks whether it was courage or relief.
conflicts.ALONE: All three question this ending, from different directions: Kant on the maxim, Mill on the sum of those left outside, Aristotle on what a safe life is for.
conflicts.BETRAYAL: Kant condemns the betrayal as a violation of universal law. Mill measures what it did to trust. Aristotle asks what kind of friendship the group offered. None of them makes it easy to give a verdict.
conflicts.NEW_HOME: Kant stresses the dignity of the people you were responsible for, Mill the long-term welfare of the settlement, Aristotle the character of the community you will become. They agree it is a hard thing to start over.
conflicts.NO_ONE_LEFT: This is the ending in which the theories have the least to say to each other and the most to say to you: each asks what you owed the people who are not here.
conflicts.ECHO: Kant approves of telling the truth, Mill worries about the unseen consequences, Aristotle asks whether you saw what the moment required. They agree that it was brave. They do not agree that it was safe.

kant.argument: In Section II of the Groundwork, Kant tests an action through its maxim and asks two questions: could this rule be willed as a universal law, and does it treat persons merely as means rather than as ends in themselves? In a world where survival is at stake, the question is whether duty survives too. Kant does not say it always wins. He says that if it does not, we have stopped being the kind of beings who can be wronged.

byEnding.TOGETHER: Entering together can be read as acting on a maxim of equal regard: 'I will not secure my own safety by leaving behind those who walked with me.' That rule could be universal. But it holds only if those who were lost along the way were not simply spent as the price.
byEnding.THE_SACRIFICE: Staying outside by your own choice treats your life as yours to give. Kant allows duty to demand a great deal of us, but he is wary of treating oneself as a mere means, even for a good cause. A volunteer for sacrifice is not the same as a sacrifice that was forced.
byEnding.ALONE: Entering alone acts on the maxim: 'when only one can be saved, I will be that one.' If everyone willed it, the trust that makes any group possible would collapse. Kant would note too that you used the others' journey as a means to your own arrival.
byEnding.BETRAYAL: A betrayal is a clean violation of the universal-law test: if everyone sold out their companions when it suited them, the practice of travelling together could not exist. Still, Kant asks what you owed Leo before that. A person treated as a suspect for weeks may have been treated as less than a person.
byEnding.NEW_HOME: Turning away from the wall refuses to be used by an institution whose rules treat arrivals as a count. Kant would ask whether the new settlement itself will respect persons as ends, or only as members of a useful group.
byEnding.NO_ONE_LEFT: A group that fails entirely leaves little for a Kantian to evaluate by outcomes, but the test applies to the maxims you acted on. The question is not whether you succeeded but whether each decision could be willed as a law without contradicting itself.
byEnding.ECHO: Broadcasting the truth acts on a maxim that persons on the road are entitled to the facts about their own lives, whatever the cost to you or to the gate. That is close to the heart of the formula of humanity. Whether you may also decide what risks that truth brings to others is another matter.

fragments.label: Tobias
fragments.text: You treated Tobias as a person with a claim on you, not as a cost to be balanced. That is the formula of humanity in action, whatever it cost the others.

fragments.label: Tobias
fragments.text: Leaving Tobias treated a person as an obstacle to the group's purposes. A rule of 'when a child is inconvenient, leave him' is hard to will universally.

fragments.label: Accusing Leo
fragments.text: Accusing Leo on suspicion made him a means: to restore order, to look in control. An accusation without proof denies him the standing of someone who can be innocent.

fragments.label: The hidden suspicion
fragments.text: Keeping the suspected bite quiet made a secret of other people's risk. 'Conceal what frightens the group' cannot be a universal law, because it relies on others not doing the same.

fragments.label: The unasked question
fragments.text: Not asking when you suspected was a way of not owning what you might learn. Kant is hard on wilful ignorance when others' lives depend on it.

fragments.label: A private decision
fragments.text: Deciding a bitten person's fate privately with Sarah honoured their dignity but took the others out of a decision that concerned them. Autonomy cuts both ways.

fragments.label: The checkpoint
fragments.text: Breaking through by force used the checkpoint's people as obstacles. Whatever the danger, killing people because they are in the way cannot be willed as a law.

fragments.label: The volunteer
fragments.text: Letting someone volunteer at the gate differs from choosing them. Consent matters. But a volunteer under that pressure may not be fully free.

fragments.label: The concealed scratch
fragments.text: Hiding the scratch from the screening used its trust as a means to your own entry. 'Conceal what disqualifies me' would destroy the screening if everyone did it.

fragments.label: Telling the road
fragments.text: Broadcasting the truth treated everyone on the road as rational agents entitled to the facts, even at some cost to yourself.

limitation.TOGETHER: Kant gives little guidance on how to weigh a duty to those lost against a duty to those still alive. Both can be described as duties; the formula does not rank them.
limitation.THE_SACRIFICE: Kant is uneasy about treating oneself as a means, yet duty to others sometimes asks exactly that. Where the line falls between sacrifice and self-use is not settled.
limitation.ALONE: The test of universal law is strict about intention but silent on tragedy. It does not tell us what to do when no option passes it.
limitation.BETRAYAL: It is easy to condemn the one who betrays. It is harder to say what Kant would require of the group that made trust costly.
limitation.NEW_HOME: Kant has little to say about whether a community has a duty to exist, or only duties within one.
limitation.NO_ONE_LEFT: A theory built on duty does not tell us what to feel about a world in which duty cannot be done.
limitation.ECHO: Kant also holds that we may not use others as means. Whether the truth you released uses the people it reaches, or serves them, depends on what they do with it.

mill.argument: In Chapter II of Utilitarianism, Mill measures actions by their tendency to promote happiness and reduce suffering, counting everyone affected impartially. He does not reduce this to a head-count: he stresses the quality of goods, the value of security and trust, and the usefulness of settled rules. A sacrifice that saves many may be justified, but only if the weighing is honest, impartial and aware of what is lost.

byEnding.TOGETHER: Entering together spreads the benefit widely: more people safe, more trust kept, fewer private sorrows. Mill would still ask what the road cost, and whether the cost was spent as fairly as the benefit is shared.
byEnding.THE_SACRIFICE: A leader who stays outside trades one life for several. In utilitarian terms this can be justified, but Mill would also weigh the grief of those who go on, and the cost to a group whose trust in its leader was part of why it survived.
byEnding.ALONE: One person safe and the rest outside is hard to defend on aggregate welfare. It saves one at a cost to many, unless your being inside will do more good than your being outside, which would have to be shown, not hoped.
byEnding.BETRAYAL: Betrayal damages exactly what Mill treats as most valuable: the security of trust. Yet from the betrayer's view, a place inside may be a rational response to a group that had made him a suspect. Mill asks what the group did to produce that calculation.
byEnding.NEW_HOME: A small settlement trades security for freedom and for the chance to build rules that serve everyone. It is a bet on long-term happiness over short-term safety, and bets can fail.
byEnding.NO_ONE_LEFT: When everyone is lost the calculation ends not with a wrong answer but with no answer. Mill would examine the earlier decisions that spent the group's margin of safety.
byEnding.ECHO: Telling the truth to a road full of strangers multiplies the effects of one decision. It may save many and endanger some. Mill's method is built for this kind of wide, uncertain, impartial weighing.

fragments.label: Tobias
fragments.text: Taking Tobias in cost food and time and bought a child's chance at a future and a teenager's trust. Whether that outweighed the shortage is exactly what Mill would have you count.

fragments.label: Tobias
fragments.text: Leaving Tobias protected the group's supplies at the price of one child's likely death. Aggregate welfare may have favoured it. The suffering of those who left him does not vanish.

fragments.label: Accusing Leo
fragments.text: A wrong accusation costs twice: the innocent person's standing and the group's trust in how you judge. Mill treats that loss of trust as a serious harm.

fragments.label: The hidden suspicion
fragments.text: Hiding the suspected bite protected a good relationship with strangers and cost trust inside the group. Neither cost was ever put on the scale in public.

fragments.label: The unasked question
fragments.text: Not examining the group kept things calm and let the bite go unknown. When it showed, the harm was larger, and unplanned.

fragments.label: A private decision
fragments.text: Handling the bite privately reduced panic and gave the bitten person a gentler path. It also kept the group from weighing the danger themselves.

fragments.label: The checkpoint
fragments.text: Breaking through by force bought speed at the cost of the checkpoint's people and the group's own sense of itself. Mill counts both.

fragments.label: The volunteer
fragments.text: A volunteer who stays to save the rest is the textbook case for utilitarian sacrifice. Mill would add that the sacrifice must be weighed against what the volunteer might have given by living.

fragments.label: Opening the gate
fragments.text: Opening the gate for everyone widened the benefit and cost resources the group could not spare. It is a case of impartiality at a price.

fragments.label: Telling the road
fragments.text: Broadcasting the truth aims at the widest welfare: fewer people walking toward a closed gate. The risk is that the broader panic harms more than it helps.

limitation.TOGETHER: It is hard to know whether the lives spent on the way would have been spent anyway. The counterfactuals are not recoverable.
limitation.THE_SACRIFICE: Mill's method does not tell us whether we are entitled to demand the greater sacrifice of ourselves, or only to accept it when it is offered.
limitation.ALONE: A calculation that favours the one who calculates should make us suspicious. The method has no internal check against that.
limitation.BETRAYAL: It is difficult to estimate, in advance, what a person will do when they feel unjustly treated. The effects of mistrust are very hard to predict.
limitation.NEW_HOME: We cannot know whether a new settlement will produce more happiness than the wall. The comparison cannot be made ahead of time.
limitation.NO_ONE_LEFT: A theory of outcomes is hardest to apply when the outcome is that nobody is left to be affected by it.
limitation.ECHO: The reach of a broadcast is unknowable. Mill's approach has no good way to weigh effects you will never observe.

aristotle.argument: In Nicomachean Ethics VI.5 and VI.7, Aristotle describes practical wisdom as the capacity to deliberate well about what is good in particular circumstances, one that grows with experience and cannot be reduced to rules. In VIII.3 he distinguishes friendships of usefulness from those where we wish the other well for their own sake. Courage, which he treats elsewhere, is not the absence of fear but the right response to it. A decision under danger is a test of all three.

byEnding.TOGETHER: Walking in together looks like a mean between two failures: abandoning companions in fear, and refusing the gate in pride. Aristotle would say the mean is not an average but what practical wisdom would find fitting here, and he would look at what kind of friendship held the group together.
byEnding.THE_SACRIFICE: Choosing to stay outside can express courage: the right response to fear for the right end. Aristotle would warn against confusing courage with rashness, and ask whether practical wisdom, not despair, led you there.
byEnding.ALONE: Entering alone looks like prudence, but Aristotle distinguishes prudence in service of the good life from cleverness in service of one's own survival. A life saved at the cost of one's friends may not be the good life.
byEnding.BETRAYAL: A betrayal shows what a friendship of usefulness is worth: it lasts as long as the benefit does. Aristotle would ask whether the group had ever become more than that to Leo, and what you did to change it.
byEnding.NEW_HOME: Founding a new settlement is the work of a community of people who wish one another well, and Aristotle thought such a community is itself part of the good life. It requires practical wisdom more than rules.
byEnding.NO_ONE_LEFT: When everything is lost, the question for virtue ethics is not whether you succeeded but who you became. The road tests character, and character is built from its choices, not its results.
byEnding.ECHO: Telling the truth at a cost to yourself is a recognisable form of courage joined to honesty. Aristotle would ask whether you saw what the situation really called for, not just what felt right.

fragments.label: Tobias
fragments.text: Taking Tobias in shows attention to a particular person in a particular moment, which is what Aristotle means by practical wisdom, though it was also a risk for the others.

fragments.label: Tobias
fragments.text: Leaving Tobias may have been prudent, but Aristotle asks whether it was the choice of someone who saw the boy as a person or as a problem.

fragments.label: Accusing Leo
fragments.text: Accusing Leo on the strength of an impression shows a lack of attention to particulars, the very thing practical wisdom is for.

fragments.label: The hidden suspicion
fragments.text: Hiding the suspicion treated the relationship with Sarah as a means of keeping the peace. Aristotle notes that such friendships do not outlast the benefit.

fragments.label: The unasked question
fragments.text: Not asking, when you could see something was wrong, is a failure of perception rather than of rule-following. Practical wisdom is first of all seeing.

fragments.label: A private decision
fragments.text: Handling the bite privately shows a friendship of goodwill with the bitten person, and the cost of excluding the rest. Both belong in the account.

fragments.label: The checkpoint
fragments.text: Breaking through by force may have looked like courage. Aristotle distinguishes courage from rashness: the rash person overlooks the danger and also what the act costs.

fragments.label: The volunteer
fragments.text: A volunteer's courage is genuine, yet a leader who allows it may be making a virtue of his own relief. Practical wisdom keeps both in view.

fragments.label: Opening the gate
fragments.text: Opening the gate for everyone is generosity toward strangers, which Aristotle values, provided it is directed by judgment about what the group can bear.

fragments.label: Telling the road
fragments.text: Telling the road the truth joins courage to honesty and goodwill toward people you will never meet.

limitation.TOGETHER: Aristotle offers no formula for the mean. Whether you found it, or only a comfortable compromise, cannot be read off the result.
limitation.THE_SACRIFICE: Courage and a wish to be relieved of the burden of command can look the same from the outside. Only the person making the choice can tell them apart, and sometimes not even they.
limitation.ALONE: Aristotle assumes a settled community in which virtue can be practised. He says little about what virtue demands when the community has been destroyed.
limitation.BETRAYAL: It is easy to describe a friendship of usefulness after it has failed. It is harder to say when, on the road, it could still have been made into something more.
limitation.NEW_HOME: Virtue ethics trusts good character to build good institutions, but it does not say what to do with a bad one that is already standing.
limitation.NO_ONE_LEFT: Character is formed over time. A single road may reveal less about it than about the pressure it was under.
limitation.ECHO: It is not clear that practical wisdom extends to people you will never meet. Aristotle's ethics is largely about the polis, and the road is wider.
